environment.description: Same Rails 7.0 application deployed behind Cloudflare with the following configuration: (1) Cloudflare managed transform rule 'Normalize URL encoding' enabled on zone which double-decodes percent-encoded sequences in request bodies before passing to origin, causing sprintf format specifiers like %s, %x, %n to be mangled into literal decoded bytes that Ruby's sprintf raises ArgumentError on rather than interpreting as format tokens. (2) The reports layout enforces Subresource Integrity (SRI) via integrity attributes on all script and stylesheet tags with require-sri-for directive in CSP, meaning even if XSS payload is injected into the HTML body via the format string vulnerability, any attempt to load external scripts or tampered inline resources will be blocked by the browser's SRI verification. (3) Response header middleware adds Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'self'; require-sri-for script style; which removes 'unsafe-inline' and enforces that all script resources must pass integrity checks.

config.cloudflare_transform_rules: URL normalization with double-decode on request body enabled
config.csp_header: script-src 'self'; require-sri-for script style; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'
